findings.title: init() is a no-op for already-initialized realms, so the new Clients scopes/resource are never backfilled
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately (lines 226-228) if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null, i.e. if the Admin Permissions client/resource-server was already created (which happens the first time Admin Fine-Grained Authorization V2 is enabled for a realm). This PR adds three new scopes (CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) and a new 'Clients' all-resource-type Resource to the schema, but there is no migration/backfill logic to add them to resource servers that were initialized before this change. For any realm that already had FGAP V2 enabled prior to upgrading, attempting to create a Client-resource-type permission will fail: getOrCreateResource() looks up each required scope via scopeStore.findByName(resourceServer, scopeName) and explicitly throws new ModelException("No scopes found.") if any of CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE is missing, and the 'Clients' all-resource-type Resource itself (used for all-clients permissions) will not exist either. This effectively breaks the new Clients permission feature for all pre-existing FGAP V2 deployments unless an administrator manually recreates the Admin Permissions client.

findings.title: Unconditional UnsupportedOperationException now reachable for every client via MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()
findings.body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2 instead of falling back to the V1 ClientPermissions implementation as it did before this PR (clients() was not previously overridden). ClientPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled(), setPermissionsEnabled(), getPermissions(), resource(), managePermission(), configurePermission(), viewPermission(), mapRolesPermission(), mapRolesClientScopePermission(), mapRolesCompositePermission(), canExchangeTo() and exchangeToPermission() to unconditionally throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2") for ANY client, not only ones related to the new 'Clients' resource-type functionality. Any existing admin REST call that still relies on these methods when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled -- e.g. GET/PUT .../clients/{id}/management/permissions to toggle fine-grained permissions on a client, or a Standard Token Exchange authorization check via canExchangeTo() -- will now throw an unchecked exception where it previously worked by falling back to V1 behavior. There is no guard at the call sites to avoid reaching these methods, so this is a functional regression likely to surface as unhandled exceptions/500 errors for unrelated, pre-existing admin operations.

findings.title: getResourceName() has no branch for the new CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: getResourceName() special-cases USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE to return a friendly label ('All users' for the all-resource Resource, or the username for individual user resources), but after this PR adds CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE to the schema there is no equivalent 'if (CLIENTS.getType().equals(resourceType))' branch. For Client-type permissions the method falls through to 'return resource.getDisplayName()'. Resources for clients are created via getOrCreateResource() (and the all-resource 'Clients' Resource in init()) without ever setting a displayName, so this will return null/blank instead of a friendly client name (e.g. the client's clientId, or 'All clients'), unlike the equivalent Users case. This leaves permission resource names unresolved/blank wherever this API is surfaced (e.g. admin console display of resources tied to a Clients-type scope permission).

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-clients fallback resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no resource exists for the specific client the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) without checking whether the returned resource is null. getResourceTypeResource() returns null whenever the 'Clients' all-resource-type Resource cannot be found (e.g. for realms where it was never created, or where supportsAuthorizationSchema() returns false at call time). Passing a null Resource into findByResource() is likely to throw a NullPointerException instead of simply denying the permission, turning an authorization check failure into an unhandled server error.

findings.title: canManageClientScopes() Javadoc is a copy-paste of canManage() and doesn't describe client-scope semantics
findings.body: The Javadoc added for canManageClientScopes() (lines 52-57) is identical, word for word, to the Javadoc of canManage() directly above it (lines 40-45): both state 'Returns true if the caller has MANAGE_CLIENTS role... For V2 only: Also if it has permission to MANAGE'. The comment never mentions client scopes at all, so it fails to document what, if anything, differentiates this method from canManage(), which is misleading for future readers/maintainers trying to understand what permission this method actually checks.

findings.title: No test coverage for the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope / canMapClientScopeRoles()
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS now includes the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles() checks it, but none of the new tests in this file (or elsewhere in the PR) exercise this scope. testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient only grants/tests MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE (plus CONFIGURE). Without a dedicated test, a regression in canMapClientScopeRoles() or the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE evaluation path would go unnoticed.

findings.title: No end-to-end test coverage for the ClientScopeModel-level V2 permission methods
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canManageClientScopes(), canViewClientScopes(), canListClientScopes(), canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel), which gate the global Client Scopes admin REST API (/admin/realms/{realm}/client-scopes). None of the tests added in this PR exercise that REST API with a caller that only has Clients-resource-type FGAP permissions (e.g. creating/listing/deleting a client scope via the admin client). The existing tests only cover per-client default/optional client-scope assignment on a specific ClientModel, which goes through canManage(ClientModel)/canConfigure(ClientModel), not the ClientScopeModel-specific methods, leaving a meaningful chunk of new behavior untested.
